Book a demo FAQs What is phishing, and how does it affect social media accounts? Phishing is a type of cyberattack where scammers trick users into providing sensitive information like passwords or credit card details. Phishing on social media often happens through fake direct messages, comments, or links that lead to fraudulent websites. What are the different types of phishing attacks? You could receive phishing emails from brand impersonators. This could include receiving a fake email from Instagram, claiming that you violated community guidelines or need to verify your identity. You or someone from your team could also fall victim to social media phishing, or angler phishing, where a scammer will pretend to be a brand’s support team, helping you resolve a query or complaint you left in the comments of a brand’s post. Some phishing attempts might even be tailored to you personally, using your name, job title or recent activity. This is called spear phishing, and can often appear more convincing because it’s a targeted attack. How can Spikerz help prevent phishing attacks on my social accounts? Spikerz acts as a mediator, cleaning up your inbox by blocking suspicious links, filtering harmful messages, and forwarding only safe and verified content. It ensures a secure experience by continuously monitoring phishing attempts across emails, text messages, and social media. How does Spikerz connect to my social accounts?
